claim: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived neural organoids display unprecedented emergent properties.
source: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived neural organoids display unprecedented emergent properties.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the broader scientific literature on neural organoids.

claim: Current organoid protocols yield tissues with multiple neuroepithelial units (neural rosettes), each acting as independent morphogenesis centers.
source: Yet in contrast to the singular neuroepithelial tube from which the entire central nervous system (CNS) develops in vivo, current organoid protocols yield tissues with multiple neuroepithelial units, a.k.a. neural rosettes, each acting as independent morphogenesis centers and thereby confounding coordinated, reproducible tissue development.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations described in the manuscript and references to existing organoid protocols.

claim: Controlling initial tissue morphology can effectively (>80%) induce single neural rosette emergence within hPSC-derived forebrain tissues.
source: Here, we discover that controlling initial tissue morphology can effectively (>80%) induce single neural rosette emergence within hPSC-derived forebrain and spinal tissues.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figure 3 and Figure 5.

claim: The optimal tissue morphology for observing singular rosette emergence was distinct for forebrain versus spinal tissues.
source: Notably, the optimal tissue morphology for observing singular rosette emergence was distinct for forebrain versus spinal tissues due to previously unknown differences in ROCK-mediated cell contractility.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing forebrain and spinal tissue rosette emergence across different micropattern sizes, as shown in Figure 5.

claim: The difference in optimal tissue morphology for forebrain versus spinal tissues is due to previously unknown differences in ROCK-mediated cell contractility.
source: Notably, the optimal tissue morphology for observing singular rosette emergence was distinct for forebrain versus spinal tissues due to previously unknown differences in ROCK-mediated cell contractility.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing differential effects of ROCK inhibition on forebrain versus spinal tissue rosette emergence, as presented in Figure 5.

claim: Following release of geometric confinement, the tissues displayed radial outgrowth with maintenance of a singular neuroepithelium.
source: Following release of geometric confinement, the tissues displayed radial outgrowth with maintenance of a singular neuroepithelium and peripheral neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and images in Figure 6 showing tissue expansion after HBP-mediated release from confinement.

claim: Following release of geometric confinement, the tissues displayed peripheral neuronal differentiation.
source: Following release of geometric confinement, the tissues displayed radial outgrowth with maintenance of a singular neuroepithelium and peripheral neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6 showing Tuj1+ neuronal cells at the tissue periphery.

claim: Human PSCs have traditionally been characterized by their ability to spontaneously recapitulate facets of developmental tissue morphogenesis upon ectopic implantation in vivo (the teratoma assay).
source: Human PSCs have traditionally been characterized by their ability to spontaneously recapitulate facets of developmental tissue morphogenesis upon ectopic implantation in vivo, that is the teratoma assay (Thomson et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Thomson et al., 1998.

claim: hPSCs can self-organize emergence of organotypic tissues in vitro, including cortical organoids.
source: However, more recent discovery of their ability to also self-organize emergence of organotypic tissues in vitro, for example cortical (Eiraku et al., 2008), retinal (Nakano et al., 2012), cerebral (Lancaster et al., 2013) and intestinal organoids (Watson et al., 2014), has spurred the creation of novel developmental and disease models with unprecedented biomimicry of microscale cytoarchitectures and cell phenotype diversity (Lancaster and Knoblich, 2014; Sasai, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Eiraku et al., 2008.

claim: hPSCs can self-organize emergence of retinal organoids in vitro.
source: However, more recent discovery of their ability to also self-organize emergence of organotypic tissues in vitro, for example cortical (Eiraku et al., 2008), retinal (Nakano et al., 2012), cerebral (Lancaster et al., 2013) and intestinal organoids (Watson et al., 2014), has spurred the creation of novel developmental and disease models with unprecedented biomimicry of microscale cytoarchitectures and cell phenotype diversity (Lancaster and Knoblich, 2014; Sasai, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nakano et al., 2012.

claim: hPSCs can self-organize emergence of cerebral organoids in vitro.
source: However, more recent discovery of their ability to also self-organize emergence of organotypic tissues in vitro, for example cortical (Eiraku et al., 2008), retinal (Nakano et al., 2012), cerebral (Lancaster et al., 2013) and intestinal organoids (Watson et al., 2014), has spurred the creation of novel developmental and disease models with unprecedented biomimicry of microscale cytoarchitectures and cell phenotype diversity (Lancaster and Knoblich, 2014; Sasai, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lancaster et al., 2013.

claim: hPSCs can self-organize emergence of intestinal organoids in vitro.
source: However, more recent discovery of their ability to also self-organize emergence of organotypic tissues in vitro, for example cortical (Eiraku et al., 2008), retinal (Nakano et al., 2012), cerebral (Lancaster et al., 2013) and intestinal organoids (Watson et al., 2014), has spurred the creation of novel developmental and disease models with unprecedented biomimicry of microscale cytoarchitectures and cell phenotype diversity (Lancaster and Knoblich, 2014; Sasai, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Watson et al., 2014.

claim: In vivo, neurulation results in emergence of a singular neuroepithelial tube that spans the entire rostrocaudal axis of the embryo's dorsal plane.
source: In vivo, neurulation results in emergence of a singular neuroepithelial tube that spans the entire rostrocaudal (R/C) axis of the embryo's dorsal plane and serves as the primordium of all CNS tissues.
evidence: This claim is based on established developmental biology knowledge.

claim: The singular neuroepithelial tube serves as the primordium of all CNS tissues.
source: In vivo, neurulation results in emergence of a singular neuroepithelial tube that spans the entire rostrocaudal (R/C) axis of the embryo's dorsal plane and serves as the primordium of all CNS tissues.
evidence: This claim is based on established developmental biology knowledge.

claim: Disruption of the neuroepithelial tube's N-cadherin polarized cytoarchitecture eliminates the sole neurogenic source of embryonic CNS development.
source: Disruption of the neuroepithelial tube's N-cadherin polarized cytoarchitecture eliminates the sole neurogenic source of embryonic CNS development (Zhang et al., 2010a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2010a.

claim: The presence of multiple neural tubes during development causes congenital abnormalities such as dipolmyelia and diastematomyelia.
source: Alternatively, the presence of multiple neural tubes during development causes congenital abnormalities such as dipolmyelia and diastematomyelia (Testoni et al., 2010; Cogliatti, 1986) or anencephaly as observed in diprosopic parapagus twins (Spencer, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Testoni et al., 2010 and Cogliatti, 1986.

claim: The presence of multiple neural tubes during development causes anencephaly as observed in diprosopic parapagus twins.
source: Alternatively, the presence of multiple neural tubes during development causes congenital abnormalities such as dipolmyelia and diastematomyelia (Testoni et al., 2010; Cogliatti, 1986) or anencephaly as observed in diprosopic parapagus twins (Spencer, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Spencer, 2000.

claim: In current 2- and 3-D hPSC-derived cultures, neurulation-like events occur spontaneously yielding uncontrolled emergence of numerous polarized neuroepithelial tissues (neural rosettes).
source: In current 2- and 3-D hPSC-derived cultures, neurulation-like events occur spontaneously yielding uncontrolled emergence of numerous polarized neuroepithelial tissues, a.k.a. neural rosettes (Lancaster et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lancaster et al., 2013 and Zhang et al., 2001.

claim: Stirred-tank bioreactor culture during 3-D neural organoid derivation can induce the formation of larger and more contiguous neuroepithelial tissues.
source: Integration of engineering techniques such as stirred-tank bioreactor culture during 3-D neural organoid derivation can induce the formation of larger and more contiguous neuroepithelial tissues (Lancaster et al., 2013; Renner et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lancaster et al., 2013 and Renner et al., 2017.

claim: Derivation of neural organoids around filamentous biomaterial scaffolds induces elongated neuroepithelial tissues within the 3-D organoid.
source: Likewise, derivation of neural organoids around filamentous biomaterial scaffolds was shown to induce elongated neuroepithelial tissues within the 3-D organoid (Lancaster et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lancaster et al., 2017.

claim: Singular neural rosette emergence was routinely observed upon derivation of 3-D neuroepithelial cysts from single cell mouse embryonic stem cell suspensions.
source: Interestingly, singular neural rosette emergence was routinely observed upon derivation of 3-D neuroepithlelial cysts, which have considerably smaller dimensions than hPSC-derived organoids and are generated from single cell mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC) suspensions (Meinhardt et al., 2014; Ranga et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Meinhardt et al., 2014 and Ranga et al., 2014.

claim: Manual isolation of singular neural rosettes from culture is the only reliable in vitro method for generating biomimetic cytoarchitecture within hPSC-derived organotypic CNS tissues.
source: Manual isolation of singular neural rosettes from culture remains the only reliable in vitro method for generating such critical biomimetic cytoarchitecture within hPSC-derived organotypic CNS tissues (Lee et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2017 and Shi et al., 2012.

claim: Geometric confinement of hPSC tissues on 2-D micropatterned substrates induces self-organized embryonic patterning in a morphology dependent manner.
source: Geometric confinement of hPSC tissues on 2-D micropatterned substrates was recently shown to induce self-organized embryonic patterning, that is mimicking gastrulation, in a morphology dependent manner (Warmflash et al., 2014; Etoc et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Warmflash et al., 2014 and Etoc et al., 2016.

claim: The E6 protocol generates near homogenous monolayers of Pax6+/Sox2+/N-cadherin+ NECs in six days without the use of SMAD inhibitors.
source: In six days and without the use of SMAD inhibitors (Chambers et al., 2009), the E6 protocol generates near homogenous monolayers of Pax6+/Sox2+/N-cadherin+ NECs that spontaneously produce cultures densely populated with neural rosettes of varying shapes and sizes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to the E6 protocol and citation to Chambers et al., 2009, as well as data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The onset of Pax6 expression began between days 2 (0%) and 3 (44 ± 15%) of the E6 protocol.
source: In agreement with previous studies (Lippmann et al., 2014), the onset of Pax6 expression, a human neuroectodermal fate determinant (Zhang et al., 2010b), began between days 2 (0%) and 3 (44 ± 15%) of the E6 protocol (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-D and citation to Lippmann et al., 2014.

claim: By day 5 of the E6 protocol, Pax6 expression had reached 81 ± 5%.
source: By day 5, Pax6 expression had reached 81 ± 5% and N-cadherin+ polarization foci had both increased in prevalence and morphed into coherent rings surrounded by contiguous alignment of polarized NECs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: By day 3 of the E6 protocol, the presence of polarized N-cadherin+ foci were observed concurrent with increasing Pax6 expression.
source: By day 3 and concurrent with increasing Pax6 expression, the presence of polarized N-cadherin+ foci were observed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Co-localization of F-actin, ZO-1 tight junction proteins, and phospho-H3+ mitotic nuclei within polarized N-cadherin structures supports the use of polarized N-cadherin as a surrogate marker of neural rosette emergence.
source: Co-localization of F-actin, ZO-1 tight junction proteins, and phospho-H3+ mitotic nuclei within these polarized structures further supports the use of polarized N-cadherin as a surrogate marker of neural rosette emergence (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) Shi et al., 2012.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and citation to Shi et al., 2012.

claim: Neural rosette emergence occurs over five days after commencing E6 culture in 6-well plates with correlated and progressive increases in Pax6 expression and N-cadherin polarization.
source: Thus, neural rosette emergence occurs over five days after commencing E6 culture in 6-well plates with correlated and progressive increases in Pax6 expression and N-cadherin polarization.
evidence: This claim is supported by the time course analysis data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The 5 day time point correlated with the highest occurrence (30%, n = 100 tissues) of singular rosette emergence within micropatterned NEC tissues.
source: The 5 day time point also correlated with the highest occurrence (30%, n = 100 tissues) of singular rosette emergence within micropatterned NEC tissues (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: NECs appear to proliferate within micropatterned tissues after seeding as indicated by increased Pax6+ cell density.
source: Additionally, the NECs appeared to proliferate within micropatterned tissues after seeding as indicated by increased Pax6+ cells density (e.g. day 7 vs 9, Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from immunostaining images in Figure 1F.

claim: In all conditions tested, cells proliferated and produced neuroepithelial tissues with at least a 2-fold increase in cell density, >80% Pax6 expression, and consistent neural rosette formation.
source: In all conditions, the cells proliferated and produced neuroepithelial tissues with at least a 2-fold increase in cell density, >80% Pax6 expression, and consistent neural rosette formation (Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D.

claim: A 5 day paradigm for neural rosette emergence in E6 media holds for cultures seeded at all stages of hESC neural induction.
source: These results indicate that a 5 day paradigm for neural rosette emergence in E6 media holds for cultures seeded at all stages of hESC neural induction and appears to be a function of Pax6 expression and local cell density.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the subculture time point experiment shown in Figure 1H-I.

claim: Neural rosette emergence appears to be a function of Pax6 expression and local cell density.
source: These results indicate that a 5 day paradigm for neural rosette emergence in E6 media holds for cultures seeded at all stages of hESC neural induction and appears to be a function of Pax6 expression and local cell density.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental observations across different seeding time points.

claim: Switching from a 9.6 cm2 (a well in a 6-well plate) to a 0.071 mm2 (300μm diameter) circular neuroepithelial tissue can substantially reduce the number of emerging neural rosettes.
source: The previous experiments demonstrated that switching from a 9.6 cm2 (a well in a 6-well plate) to a 0.071 mm2 (300μm diameter) circular neuroepithelial tissue can substantially reduce the number of emerging neural rosettes.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of data from well plate culture (Figure 1) and micropatterned culture experiments.

claim: 0.031mm2 circular (56%) and square (57%) morphologies were the most efficient at inducing '1 Rosette' neuroepithelial tissues based on manual analysis.
source: Although all micropatterned tissue morphologies exhibited the capacity to induce '1 Rosette' neuroepithelial tissues, 0.031mm2 circular (56%) and square (57%) morphologies were the most efficient.
evidence: This claim is supported by manual quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The automated workflow estimated lower percentages of singular rosette emergence efficiency across all tissue morphologies compared to manual assessment.
source: Compared to manual assessment, image analysis using the automated workflow estimated lower percentages of singular rosette emergence efficiency across all tissue morphologies (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of data in Figure 2B (manual) and Figure 2D (automated).

claim: The classifier's rosette identification error rate is primarily due to false positives (erroneously classifying a polarization foci as rosette).
source: This was expected since the classifier's rosette identification error rate is primarily due to false positives, that is erroneously classifying a polarization foci as rosette (Table S2).
evidence: This claim is supported by error analysis data in Table S2.

claim: The probability of biomimetic, singular rosette emergence increased as the neuroepithelial tissue's surface area decreased.
source: The probability of biomimetic, singular rosette emergence increased as the neuroepithelial tissue's surface area decreased.
evidence: This claim is supported by the trend observed in automated analysis data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 200 μm diameter (0.031 mm2) circular morphologies are more efficient at inducing singular rosette emergence than square or triangle morphologies (48.9% vs. 29.9% vs. 31.2% respectively).
source: Interestingly, the automated analysis of increased sample size suggests that 200 μm diameter (0.031 mm2) circular versus square or triangle morphologies is more efficient at inducing singular rosette emergence, that is 48.9% vs. 29.9% vs. 31.2% respectively (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by automated quantification data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Tissues formed using Pax6- D1-2 cultures versus Pax6+ D3-5 cultures displayed a significant increase in neuroepithelial cell density.
source: In Figure 1's rosette emergence characterization experiments, it was also noted that tissues formed using Pax6- D1-2 cultures versus Pax6+ D3-5 cultures displayed a significant increase in neuroepithelial cell density (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell density quantification data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Manual analysis revealed a singular neural rosette emergence efficiency of 80.0 ± 0.05% vs. 38.6 ± 4.7% for neuroepithelial tissues formed by seeding D-1 hESCs vs. D4 NECs, respectively.
source: Manual analysis of over 100 neuroepithelial tissues in each experiment revealed a singular neural rosette emergence efficiency of 80.0 ± 0.05% vs. 38.6 ± 4.7% for neuroepithelial tissues formed by seeding D-1 hESCs vs. D4 NECs, respectively (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by manual quantification data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The average cell density of neuroepithelial tissues formed using D-1 hESCs vs. D4 NECs was ~1.25 fold higher after 5 days of E6 culture (149 ± 23 vs. 119 ± 18 cells respectively).
source: The average cell density of neuroepithelial tissues formed using D-1 hESCs vs. D4 NECs was ~1.25 fold higher after 5 days of E6 culture or ~30 more cells per tissue, that is 149 ± 23 vs. 119 ± 18 cells respectively (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell density quantification data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: E6 culture of hESCs on 200 μm diameter (0.031 mm2) circular micropatterns induces reproducible, singular rosette emergence within forebrain neuroepithelial tissues in part due to their increased proliferative capacity.
source: Thus, E6 culture of hESCs on 200 μm diameter (0.031 mm2) circular micropatterns induces reproducible, singular rosette emergence within forebrain neuroepithelial tissues in part due to their increased proliferative capacity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing D-1 hESC and D4 NEC-derived tissues in Figure 3.

claim: Singular rosette tissues derived from D-1 hESCs exhibited apico-basal polarity from a wider, central N-cadherin ring.
source: Singular rosettes tissues derived from D-1 hESCs exhibited apico-basal polarity from a wider, central N-cadherin ring, while D4 NEC-derived singular rosette tissues had a tighter N-cadherin ring and appeared to have contracted slightly from their initial boundary (Figure 3B,E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations from immunostaining images in Figure 3B, E, and F.

claim: D4 NEC-derived singular rosette tissues had a tighter N-cadherin ring and appeared to have contracted slightly from their initial boundary.
source: Singular rosettes tissues derived from D-1 hESCs exhibited apico-basal polarity from a wider, central N-cadherin ring, while D4 NEC-derived singular rosette tissues had a tighter N-cadherin ring and appeared to have contracted slightly from their initial boundary (Figure 3B,E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations from immunostaining images in Figure 3B, E, and F.

claim: NECs derived using the E6 protocol pattern to a default Pax6+/Otx2+ dorsal forebrain phenotype both in well plate and micropatterned tissue culture.
source: NECs derived using the E6 protocol pattern to a default Pax6+/Otx2+ dorsal forebrain phenotype both in well plate and micropatterned tissue culture (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 3B and reference to the E6 protocol.

claim: The HOX patterning protocol enables derivation of NECs of discrete hindbrain through spinal cord regional phenotypes via deterministic patterning of their HOX expression profiles.
source: We have also published a protocol for deriving NECs of discrete hindbrain through spinal cord regional phenotypes via deterministic patterning of their HOX expression profiles (Lippmann et al., 2015) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lippmann et al., 2015 and schematic in Figure 4A.

claim: The HOX patterning protocol begins with high density seeding of hPSCs followed by induction of a stable neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP) phenotype using sequential activation of FGF8b and Wnt signaling.
source: The protocol begins with high density seeding of hPSCs (D-1) followed by induction of a stable neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP) phenotype using sequential activation of FGF8b and Wnt signaling.
evidence: This claim describes the HOX patterning protocol methodology.

claim: Upon addition of the Wnt agonist (CHIR), HOX expression activates in a colinear and combinatorial manner over 7 days.
source: Upon addition of the Wnt agonist (CHIR), HOX expression activates in a colinear and combinatorial manner over 7 days.
evidence: This claim describes the temporal dynamics of HOX expression in the protocol.

claim: The optimal protocol regimen for spinal neuroepithelial tissues consisted of seeding spinal NMPs at 2.5 × 10^5 cells/cm2 onto micropatterned substrates, culturing in RA supplemented E6 media for 72 hr, and applying a 6 hr, 6.0 μM Wnt boost immediately prior to 96 hr of 0.5 μg/mL SHH and 0.5 μM PM exposure.
source: Manual tissue analysis in each condition revealed that the optimal protocol regimen consisted of seeding spinal NMPs at 2.5 × 105 cells/cm2 onto micropatterned substrates, culturing in RA supplemented E6 media for 72 hr, and applying a 6 hr, 6.0 μM Wnt boost immediately prior to 96 hr of 0.5 μg/mL SHH and 0.5 μM PM exposure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental optimization data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The optimal spinal protocol regimen consistently yielded both good cell viability and tissue formation as well as effective ventral patterning (86 ± 11% Nkx6.1+/Olig2+).
source: Waiting 72 hr after NMP seeding before applying the Wnt boost followed by SHH/PM exposure was the only tested regimen that consistently yielded both good cell viability and tissue formation as well as effective ventral patterning, that is 86 ± 11% (n = 8) Nkx6.1+/Olig2+ (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Only ~12% (n = 97) of spinal neuroepithelial tissues on 200 μm diameter (0.031 mm2) circular micropatterns displayed singular rosette emergence.
source: Yet, only ~12% (n = 97) of neuroepithelial tissues on 200 μm diameter (0.031 mm2) circular micropatterns displayed singular rosette emergence (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Singular neural rosette emergence within forebrain tissues peaked at 85% on 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter circular micropatterns.
source: Similar to our previous results, the efficiency of singular neural rosette emergence for forebrain tissues peaked at 85% on 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter circular micropatterns (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency of singular rosette emergence in forebrain tissues was 75% vs. 0% on 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter micropatterns.
source: However, in the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency curve shifted leftward inducing singular rosette emergence in 75% vs. 0% of 150 μm (0.018 mm2), 89% vs. 50% of 180 μm (0.025 mm2), 87% vs. 58% of 200 μm (0.031 mm2), and 11% vs. 85% of 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter forebrain neuroepithelial tissues, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency of singular rosette emergence in forebrain tissues was 89% vs. 50% on 180 μm (0.025 mm2) diameter micropatterns.
source: However, in the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency curve shifted leftward inducing singular rosette emergence in 75% vs. 0% of 150 μm (0.018 mm2), 89% vs. 50% of 180 μm (0.025 mm2), 87% vs. 58% of 200 μm (0.031 mm2), and 11% vs. 85% of 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter forebrain neuroepithelial tissues, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency of singular rosette emergence in forebrain tissues was 87% vs. 58% on 200 μm (0.031 mm2) diameter micropatterns.
source: However, in the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency curve shifted leftward inducing singular rosette emergence in 75% vs. 0% of 150 μm (0.018 mm2), 89% vs. 50% of 180 μm (0.025 mm2), 87% vs. 58% of 200 μm (0.031 mm2), and 11% vs. 85% of 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter forebrain neuroepithelial tissues, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency of singular rosette emergence in forebrain tissues was 11% vs. 85% on 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter micropatterns.
source: However, in the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor, the efficiency curve shifted leftward inducing singular rosette emergence in 75% vs. 0% of 150 μm (0.018 mm2), 89% vs. 50% of 180 μm (0.025 mm2), 87% vs. 58% of 200 μm (0.031 mm2), and 11% vs. 85% of 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter forebrain neuroepithelial tissues, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Singular neural rosette emergence within spinal neuroepithelial tissues peaked at 73.5% on 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter micropatterns.
source: In comparison, singular neural rosette emergence within spinal neuroepithelial tissues peaked at 73.5% on 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter micropatterns, and the presence of ROCK inhibitor completely abolished their ability to form neural rosettes (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The presence of ROCK inhibitor completely abolished the ability of spinal neuroepithelial tissues to form neural rosettes.
source: In comparison, singular neural rosette emergence within spinal neuroepithelial tissues peaked at 73.5% on 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter micropatterns, and the presence of ROCK inhibitor completely abolished their ability to form neural rosettes (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: NEC density within forebrain vs. spinal tissues of a given micropattern size and in the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor did not vary significantly.
source: Of note, NEC density within forebrain vs. spinal tissues of a given micropattern size and in the presence vs. absence of ROCK inhibitor did not vary significantly (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell density quantification data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The optimal morphology for single neural rosette emergence in forebrain neuroepithelial tissues is 200–250 μm (0.031–0.049 mm2) diameter circular micropatterns.
source: Considering our previous experiment (Figure 3), the optimal morphology for single neural rosette emergence in forebrain and spinal neuroepithelial tissues is 200–250 μm (0.031–0.049 mm2) and 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter circular micropatterns respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data across Figures 3 and 5.

claim: The optimal morphology for single neural rosette emergence in spinal neuroepithelial tissues is 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter circular micropatterns.
source: Considering our previous experiment (Figure 3), the optimal morphology for single neural rosette emergence in forebrain and spinal neuroepithelial tissues is 200–250 μm (0.031–0.049 mm2) and 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter circular micropatterns respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: The physical size of emergent neural rosettes is not conserved across tissues of increasing area.
source: The physical size of emergent neural rosettes is not conserved across tissues of increasing area (Figure 5B and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from images in Figure 5B and E.

claim: The micropatterned tissue morphology does not instruct rosette morphogenesis, but restricts tissue area to statistically favor emergence of a single rosette in accordance with innate NEC properties.
source: Hence, the micropatterned tissue morphology does not instruct rosette morphogenesis, but restricts tissue area to statistically favor emergence of a single rosette in accordance with innate NEC properties.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that rosette size varies independently of tissue size.

claim: ROCK inhibition down-regulates actin polymerization and actomyosin contraction.
source: Since ROCK inhibition down-regulates actin polymerization and actomyosin contraction (Amano et al., 2010), the results in Figure 5 imply that decreasing the contractility of forebrain NECs reduces the length scale over which the cells can effectively polarize to evoke a rosette structure, that is 250 μm vs. 150/180/200 μm in 0 vs. 10 μM Rock inhibitor.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Amano et al., 2010.

claim: Decreasing the contractility of forebrain NECs reduces the length scale over which the cells can effectively polarize to evoke a rosette structure.
source: Since ROCK inhibition down-regulates actin polymerization and actomyosin contraction (Amano et al., 2010), the results in Figure 5 imply that decreasing the contractility of forebrain NECs reduces the length scale over which the cells can effectively polarize to evoke a rosette structure, that is 250 μm vs. 150/180/200 μm in 0 vs. 10 μM Rock inhibitor.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the ROCK inhibition experimental results in Figure 5.

claim: Forebrain NECs can generate more contractile force than spinal NECs since singular rosette emergence peaks in larger forebrain (250 μm diameter) versus smaller spinal (150 μm diameter) circular tissues.
source: This further suggests that forebrain vs. spinal NECs can generate more contractile force since singular rosette emergence peaks in larger forebrain, that is 250 μm (0.049 mm2) diameter, versus smaller spinal, that is 150 μm (0.018 mm2) diameter, circular tissues.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential optimal micropattern sizes for forebrain vs. spinal tissues.

claim: The ability of 10 μM Rock inhibitor to only partially diminish vs. fully eliminate the rosette formation capacity of forebrain vs. spinal NECs supports the ranking of contractility (forebrain > spinal).
source: The ability of 10 μM Rock inhibitor to only partially diminish vs. fully eliminate the rosette formation capacity of forebrain vs. spinal NECs also supports this ranking of contractility.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential effects of ROCK inhibition on forebrain vs. spinal tissues shown in Figure 5.

claim: NEC biomechanical properties vary based on their regional patterning.
source: These results provide the first evidence that NEC biomechanical properties vary based on their regional patterning.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential responses of forebrain and spinal NECs to micropattern size and ROCK inhibition.

claim: PEG-brushes modified in situ with 10 μM HBP-DBCO bioconjugate are capable of immobilizing Laminin proteins.
source: Thus, PEG-brushes modified in situ with 10 μM HBP-DBCO bioconjugate are capable of immobilizing Laminin proteins, and potentially a diverse cadre of basement membrane ECM proteins that bind heparin sulfate proteoglycans (Sarrazin et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3 and citation to Sarrazin et al., 2011.

claim: On reactive substrates modified in situ with HBP-DBCO bioconjugates, the tissues expanded as coherent, multilayered structures maintaining a singular neuroepithelium.
source: In contrast, on reactive substrates modified in situ with HBP-DBCO bioconjugates, the tissues expanded as a coherent, multilayered structures maintaining a singular neuroepithelium and eventually intersecting with neighboring tissues.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations and images in Figure 6.

claim: Tissues on reactive substrates displayed basal deposition of laminin resembling the developing neural tube's basal lamina.
source: Also, they displayed basal deposition of laminin resembling the developing neural tube's basal lamina (Figure 6C–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6C-D.

claim: Expanded tissues maintained a singular Pax6+ neuroepithelium throughout the culture period that morphed into a 3-D hemispherical structure with a central cavity.
source: These tissues also maintained a singular Pax6+ neuroepithelium throughout the culture period that morphed into a 3-D hemispherical structure with a central cavity and Tuj1+ neuronal cells residing at the tissue's periphery (Figure 6F–G and Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6F-G.

claim: Expanded tissues displayed Tuj1+ neuronal cells residing at the tissue's periphery.
source: These tissues also maintained a singular Pax6+ neuroepithelium throughout the culture period that morphed into a 3-D hemispherical structure with a central cavity and Tuj1+ neuronal cells residing at the tissue's periphery (Figure 6F–G and Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6F-G.

claim: Controlled induction of singular rosette emergence upon organotypic neural tissue formation will persist throughout subsequent stages of morphogenesis.
source: These results indicate that controlled induction of singular rosette emergence upon organotypic neural tissue formation will persist throughout subsequent stages of morphogenesis, thereby enabling formation of a biomimetic nascent CNS tissue cytoarchitecture.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing maintenance of singular rosette structure during tissue expansion in Figure 6.

claim: A consistent limitation in creating reproducible and biomimetic neural organoid anatomy at the macroscale is the random formation of multiple polarized neuroepithelial regions (rosettes).
source: However, a consistent limitation in creating reproducible and biomimetic neural organoid anatomy at the macroscale is the random formation of multiple polarized neuroepithelial regions, a.k.a. rosettes, which can each act as independent morphogenesis centers.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of current limitations in organoid technology.

claim: Enforcing a 200 – 250 μm forebrain and 150 μm spinal, circular, neuroepithelial tissue morphology optimally induces formation of a singular rosette cytoarchitecture with 80 – 85% and 73.5% efficiency respectively.
source: Using micropatterned culture substrates, we have demonstrated that enforcing a 200 – 250 μm forebrain and 150 μm spinal, circular, neuroepithelial tissue morphology optimally induces formation of a singular rosette cytoarchitecture with 80 – 85% and 73.5% efficiency respectively (Figures 3 and 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: The biophysical parameters for reproducible induction of a biomimetic, neural tube-like cytoarchitecture are dependent on local cell density, acquisition of Pax6 expression, and cell autonomous biomechanical properties such as contractility.
source: Our results indicate that these biophysical parameters for reproducible induction of a biomimetic, neural tube-like cytoarchitecture are dependent on local cell density, acquisition of Pax6 expression, and cell autonomous biomechanical properties such as contractility.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the collective experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Micropatterned E6 differentiation of D90A SOD1 mutant ALS-iPSCs showed optimal singular, forebrain rosette emergence within 250 μm diameter circular tissues but at a lower (26%) efficiency.
source: Interestingly, while these results were consistent for tested hESC lines, micropatterned E6 differentiation of D90A SOD1 mutant ALS-iPSCs also showed optimal singular, forebrain rosette emergence within 250 μm diameter circular tissues but at a lower (26%) efficiency (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Line-to-line variations in neural induction efficiency must be overcome for effective micropatterning of singular neural rosette emergence.
source: This corresponded to many instances where tissues displayed a non-uniform Pax6+ NEC phenotype, indicating that line-to-line variations in neural induction efficiency must be overcome for effective micropatterning of singular neural rosette emergence.
evidence: This claim is inferred from observations with the ALS-iPSC line.

claim: The singular neural rosette cytoarchitecture can be maintained upon subsequent tissue morphogenesis.
source: Furthermore, we have shown that the singular neural rosette cytoarchitecture can be maintained upon subsequent tissue morphogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Initial constraint of tissue morphology in accordance with identified length scales could be a generalizable approach to engineering human neural organoids with standardized nascent CNS tissue cytoarchitecture.
source: This indicates that initial constraint of tissue morphology in accordance with these identified length scales could be a generalizable approach to engineering human neural organoids with standardized nascent CNS tissue cytoarchitecture.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the experimental results.

claim: Micropatterned tissues morph from 2-D monolayers into 3-D hemispherical tissues.
source: However, we acknowledge that our micropatterned tissue do morph from 2-D monolayers into 3-D hemispherical tissues (Figure 6), and therefore, our identified optimal tissue morphology parameters may not be precisely conserved for organoids initially formed as 3-D cell aggregates.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations in Figure 6.

claim: The biomechanical properties of Pax6+/N-cadherin+ NECs of the dorsal forebrain differ from those of the ventral spinal cord.
source: In efforts to develop a unified approach for inducing singular neural rosette emergence within neuroepithelium patterned to any CNS rostrocaudal region, we discovered that the biomechanical properties of Pax6+/N-cadherin+ NECs of the dorsal forebrain differed from those of the ventral spinal cord.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: Forebrain NECs appear to be able to form a singular neural rosette within tissue of larger circular dimensions than spinal NECs because of their increased contractility.
source: Forebrain NECs appear to be able to form a singular neural rosette within tissue of larger circular dimensions than spinal NECs because of their increased contractility (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: The difference in optimal tissue dimensions for forebrain vs. spinal NECs correlates with the significantly larger dimensions of forebrain ventricles versus the spinal cord's central canal.
source: This would seem to correlate with the significantly larger dimensions of forebrain ventricles versus the spinal cord's central canal, and could represent a novel axis between the biochemical morphogens and biomechanical properties that govern CNS morphogenesis.
evidence: This claim is speculative, drawing a connection between in vitro observations and in vivo anatomy.

claim: The experimental paradigm provides a unique platform for analysis of the interplay between biochemical and biomechanical factors that govern neural rosette formation.
source: While our conclusions are based on observations from correlated perturbations of ROCK activity and not direct contractility measurements, our experimental paradigm does provide a unique platform for further definitive analysis of the interplay between biochemical and biomechanical factors that govern this facet of human CNS morphogenesis.
evidence: This claim is speculative about future applications of the platform.

claim: There is no other experimentally tractable means by which neural rosette formation phenomena can be investigated within a human genomic background.
source: To our knowledge, there is no other experimentally tractable means by which such phenomena can be investigated within a human genomic background.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: The 3-D nature of organoids grown in suspension culture limits real-time analysis of internal morphogenesis processes using traditional imaging modalities.
source: The 3-D nature of organoids grown in suspension culture provides constituent cells with a biomimetic tissue context. However, suspension organoids grow to millimeters in diameter limiting real-time analysis of internal morphogenesis processes using traditional imaging modalities.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of limitations of suspension organoid culture.

claim: Microarrayed neural tissues become definitively 3-D (>4 cell layers thick) within 4 days of culture and continue to increase in thickness upon extended culture.
source: While our microarrayed neural tissues initiate as a 2-D monolayer, they quickly become multilayered and definitively 3-D, that is >4 cell layers thick, within 4 days of culture and continue to increase in thickness upon extended culture (Figures 3 and 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations in Figures 3 and 6.

claim: The biophysical and electrophysiological benefits of 3-D organoids may apply within engineered neural tube slides.
source: Thus, the biophysical (Khetan et al., 2013) and electrophysiological (Frega et al., 2014) benefit of 3-D organoids may still apply within our engineered neural tube slides.
evidence: This claim is speculative, supported by citations to Khetan et al., 2013 and Frega et al., 2014.

claim: The arrayed approach enables constant monitoring throughout the tissues' morphogenesis process using confocal microscopy.
source: Also, our arrayed approach enables constant monitoring throughout the tissues' morphogenesis process using confocal microscopy.
evidence: This claim is based on the technical capabilities of the micropatterned platform.

claim: WA09 (H9) and HUES3 Hb9::GFP hESCs were obtained from WiCell and the Harvard Stem Cell Institute, respectively.
source: WA09 (H9) and HUES3 Hb9::GFP hESCs were obtained from WiCell and the Harvard Stem Cell Institute, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about cell line sources.

claim: D90A SOD1 mutant ALS-iPSCs were obtained from the NINDS Cell Repository.
source: D90A SOD1 mutant ALS-iPSCs were obtained from the NINDS Cell Repository.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about cell line sources.

claim: All cell lines were authenticated as karyotypically normal by the provider.
source: All lines were authenticated as karotypically normal by the provider, used for no more than 15 passages from receipt, and were tested for mycoplasma with negative results (Charles River and WiCell).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about cell line authentication.

claim: All cell lines were tested for mycoplasma with negative results.
source: All lines were authenticated as karotypically normal by the provider, used for no more than 15 passages from receipt, and were tested for mycoplasma with negative results (Charles River and WiCell).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about quality control testing.
